subject: Performance qualification: streaming SLOs, harness handoff
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcart.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@brightcart.com
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SLOs, traffic profile and methodology ask

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team and I found the streaming demo very helpful. We discussed internal targets on the call but want to make them explicit so your benchmarking can align with our expectations. High-level asks: 

- Latency requirement: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for single-turn user prompts (payloads ~120 tokens).
- Streaming responsiveness: first token emitted within 70ms and consistent chunk cadence thereafter for streaming clients.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline of 300 concurrent active sessions with burst to 1,200 for peak windows; sustained average QPS from our edge ~420 requests/s.
- KV cache behavior: our app relies on prefix reuse; we expect ~40% prefix hit-rate at 10s TTL.

Could you share the benchmark methodology you plan to run, including the prompt set you intend to use (we can provide ours as well), the harness configuration, and the exact measurement definitions (how you compute p95, what constitutes a streaming chunk, whether warmup is included, etc.)?

I attached a short prompt deck and a sample traffic profile. We can make engineers available next week for a 60-minute handoff. Also confirm whether Redwood will run the harness in our account (preferred) or in your lab.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Senior Product Manager — Conversational AI
BrightCart

Attachments: brightcart_prompt_deck_v1.pdf, traffic_profile_sample.json
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs, traffic profile and methodology ask

Emily — really helpful list, thank you. Recap + initial plan below so we have a single source of truth before the handoff call.

Recap of BrightCart targets (as we heard them):
- p95 generation latency target: <= 350ms (single-turn, ~120 tokens)
- streaming first-token latency: <= 70ms; consistent chunk cadence for subsequent tokens
- concurrency/throughput: baseline 300 concurrent active sessions, burst to 1,200; avg ~420 rps from edge
- prefix reuse (KV cache): expected ~40% hit-rate (10s TTL)

What we will deliver ahead of the handoff:
1) Benchmark methodology doc that defines measurement windows, warmup, sampling frequency, and exact metric definitions (we compute p95 on per-request end-to-end latencies, excluding warmup period; streaming first-token is measured from request arrival to first-frame emission).
2) Harness config file we will run against your account (redwood_harness_config.yaml) — includes concurrency profiles, tokenization settings, and seed prompt bundle mapping.
3) Prompt deck sync: we'll map our canonical prompt variants to your deck and add guardrails for non-deterministic outputs.

Questions / clarifications we need from BrightCart before we run anything:
- Will you host the harness agents inside your VPC (preferred) or want Redwood to run from our lab? If within your VPC, we need a short-run IAM scope and sample instance types to validate network egress.
- For streaming, please confirm whether the client needs per-chunk timestamps or if first-token + periodic heartbeats are sufficient for your telemetry.
- Can you provide a small set (10–20) of representative long-running sessions that exercise context growth so we can validate KV caching behavior?

Attached: redwood_harness_config.yaml (draft). Proposed next steps: 60-min handoff Wed 2027-08-25 10:00 PT with your engineering lead + ours.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_harness_config.yaml
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcart.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs, traffic profile and methodology ask

Emily — quick technical addendum from the bench team. A few specifics so the measurements are reproducible and map to your production behavior: 

Measurement definitions (proposed):
- p95 generation latency: compute on completed requests after warmup; measurement window = 5 minutes samples every 1s; include both CPU+GPU queuing and model compute.
- Streaming first-token: measured from request ingress on the same host that executes model inference to first byte of stream payload; network RTT from BrightCart edge should be reported as a separate signal so we can isolate infra vs. model emission latency.
- Chunk cadence: define chunk size (token count) and maximum inter-chunk gap tolerated (we propose 150ms).

Harness details we will use:
- Tokenization: use same tokenizer/version you run in prod (please confirm). We will run both greedy and sampling modes if you have sampling enabled in prod.
- Cache priming: the harness will simulate prefix reuse at configurable hit rates — please supply representative sequences (we can also synthesize based on the deck).
- Concurrency profile: we will run multi-stage test: 1) steady-state ramp to 300 active sessions; 2) 30m soak at 420 rps; 3) 15m burst ramp to 1,200 concurrent; 4) recovery period.

Artifacts we will hand you after the run: raw latency traces (per-request), aggregated metrics (p50/p90/p95/p99), per-chunk timing for streaming sessions, and a reproducibility script that replays the exact seed and harness config for a second-run.

One operational note: to validate KV cache behavior we need either (A) the ability to run the harness from within your VPC (so cache keys land on the same endpoint you use) or (B) a short-lived synthetic dataset we can seed on the test endpoint. Option A is preferred for fidelity.

If those definitions look good, please confirm tokenization version and whether you have any extra headers (auth/tenant) we must include in the harness requests.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcart.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@brightcart.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs, traffic profile and methodology ask

Thanks Vanessa and Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick replies inline and next steps: 

- Host harness: BrightCart prefers Redwood to run the harness inside our Azure subscription for fidelity. I will follow up with cloud contacts to supply a short-lived service principal and the minimal IAM role.
- Tokenizer: we use 'tok-v3' across our inference fleet — attaching a small export of canonical tokenization metadata.
- Per-chunk telemetry: first-token + per-chunk timestamps are best for our observability; we will ingest both (your per-request traces + our edge RTT).
- Representative sessions: attached a zipped set of 12 user-session traces that exercise cart updates, multi-turn clarifications, and long receipts (these are sanitized).

Scheduling: Wed 2027-08-25 10:00 PT works for our eng lead (Alicia) and me. Please include the run/playback owner so we can agree on the validation checklist on the call.

Deliverables we expect after the run: run artifacts (traces + aggregated metrics), the reproducibility script, and a short readout doc that maps our targets to actual measured SLOs with recommendations (tuning + quantization tradeoffs if needed).

I'll upload the service principal details to the Drive link and share an internal tracker (HubSpot deal BC-2023-047). Thanks again — talk Wednesday.

—Emily
